🇺🇸 🇮🇷 Washington weighs assassinating Iran's leadership: NBC Trump administration officials are internally debating whether the US military should target senior Iranian leaders to remove so-called "hardliners." NBC News cites a US official and a person familiar with the discussions. Supporters argue the killings would show Iran's remaining leaders that Washington can find and kill them at will. They say that would give Trump a way to end the nine-month war. Opponents warn it would push whoever is left in Tehran to dig in harder and would wreck US "credibility" in future negotiations. US military leaders have also cautioned that it could put American officials at greater risk of retaliation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved to a military base near Washington over "Iranian threats." According to the sources, killing Iranian leaders has long been on the list of options presented to Trump. It has drawn renewed attention in recent weeks as he looks for a way out of the war. No final decision has been made. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Estonia Estonian Prime Minister Michal announced that closing the border with Russia would cost regional municipalities up to 600,000 euros annually. According to preliminary estimates, local self-governments may lose between 500,000 and 600,000 euros per year. Minister for Regional Affairs Sterres stated at a press conference that within two weeks he will present a package of measures for Southeast Estonia to the government. His initial assessment indicates costs in the millions of euros, though the exact sum depends on the necessary actions. The full consequences remain unclear, particularly regarding employment levels and the need to reorganise operations in several state institutions located in these regions. @Slavyangrad
